purpose: Retest the frozen temporal_viewpos_z candidate with CARLA native weather after visual QA showed that Low renderer quality did not produce valid fog visibility loss.

supersedes.reason: Low renderer quality (sg.EffectsQuality=0) produced global darkening without meaningful distance-dependent fog; no v1 feature report was completed.

renderer.name: CARLA-0.9.15-native-weather
renderer.visual_preflight_pass_definition: fog_heavy must visibly reduce distant-scene detail rather than merely darken the whole image; fog_light must be intermediate; camera/world geometry must remain paired

score.name: temporal_viewpos_z
score.clean_calibrator: 560 clean frames / 35 B2D routes from the immutable teacher560 shard

checks: fog_heavy score mean > fog_light score mean
score versus paired-clean patch-delta Spearman >= 0.10 at both fog levels
score AUROC for the top 20 percent paired-delta patches >= 0.60 at both fog levels
paired-clean delta mean is positive and fog_heavy > fog_light
fog_heavy > fog_light > clear score mean independently on both routes

decision.pass: The temporal target becomes eligible for a separate adapter-training preregistration; no training starts automatically.
decision.fail: Do not train the adapter. Treat temporal consistency as one component only and design a multi-source target for persistent appearance degradation.

claim_boundary: This is a native-renderer observation-signal gate, not evidence of task relevance, closed-loop safety, real-weather coverage, or VLM understanding.
